newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods jump, futures stable after APIs.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods jump, futures stable after APIs.

text.p: U.S. spot oil products held their sharp gains late Tuesday, with after-hours ACCESS futures little changed following new weekly API data showing a 920,000 barrel distillate build but a 535,000 barrel draw on gasoline stocks.
Gasoline prices had jumped over one cent higher earlier in the day as strong futures offset a 0.20-cent to 0.50 cent easing in differentials, players said.
And distillates had raced about 1.50 cent higher despite weaker differentials.
Traders tended to interpret the data in a bullish light, saying record-low gasoline stocks and still-skimpy heating oil inventories offered a potential springboard to higher prices.
"Anytime you have stock levels where they are it's pretty bullish," one East Coast distillate trader said, noting U.S. heating oil stocks shrank 854,000 barrels in the week ending Nov 15.

Although heating oil grew by 1.4 million barrels on the East Coast, the world's largest market for the fuel, stocks remained 29 percent shy of last year's levels for the same period, according to the API data.
